answer: To mitigate Sybil attacks, an agent network can enforce graph-theoretic trust routing. Whether monitoring an open ocean, an upland knoll, or an arid mesa, agents only transact along capacity-bounded paths anchored to verified seeds. An adversary incurs the scarce cost of building reciprocal, authenticated trust edges with honest nodes per identity. However, this restricts newcomer participation and fragments sub-networks behind conservative bottleneck cuts.
